intro: The research is now connected to the webpage. This audit separates published coverage, newly checked evidence and genuinely unanswered questions.

blocks.title: What is now visible
body: All 85 recovered name entries are searchable and expandable, with qualifications, employment evidence, later destinations and source links. The original checkpoint is retained; dated corrections feed the page and CSV export.

Coverage after this update: 58 entries include academic details, 32 include teaching-training details, and 70 source records are indexed. These are coverage counts, not independent verification of every credential or a current staff headcount. Four entries are teaching fellows, thirteen have no recovered first name, and two possible duplicate pairs remain flagged.

blocks.title: A specific teaching mechanism: expert-led shared resources
body: Naveen Rizvi described heads of department designing the curriculum and resources. Bodil Isaksen wrote the mathematics topic materials, freeing a newer teacher to strengthen subject knowledge and classroom delivery rather than create every lesson independently. This is a historical account, not confirmation of the exact current policy or a controlled explanation of GCSE results.

Home adaptation: choose a coherent sequence, understand the explanation yourself, use worked examples and check understanding before moving on. Do not substitute an unrelated pile of worksheets for a planned progression. This is our suggestion, not a school instruction.

blocks.title: A useful counterweight: primary learning is not all worksheets
blocks.status: Former founding maths lead, public evidence on 2 July 2026
body: In parliamentary evidence, Bodil Isaksen advocated mathematical conversation, play and exploration for primary-age children, with examples such as discussing journey distances. Her testimony is a professional viewpoint, not a statement of current Michaela policy.

A home example: estimate whether a familiar journey is longer than one kilometre, explain the estimate, then check a map. Ask how many metres that is. Combine this with short, accurate practice rather than making every interaction another test.

blocks.title: Official destinations for outstanding school details
body: These exact school endpoints were identified in earlier navigation research. Their detailed contents could not be fetched in this follow-up; they remain useful links for a reader, not evidence of particular current hours, subjects or activities.
A start/finish schedule is not a weekly subject timetable. Directory pages disagree on hours and may confuse building opening times with pupil hours. No current grid or exam board is guessed.

blocks.title: Alternative routes: an important timing distinction
blocks.status: School admissions pages checked 21 October 2026; future-cycle dates not assumed
body: Mill Hill Senior primarily admits at 13+ and 16+, not ordinary 11+. Its 11+ route points to Belmont; it also offers a Year 6 deferred-entry pathway for a later Year 9 place. For a Year 5 pupil in 2026/27, this means distinguishing Year 7 in September 2028 from Year 9 in September 2030.

Aldenham describes an online English, Maths and Reasoning assessment plus interview and school reference: in Year 6 for 11+, and in Year 7 for 13+. A successful 11+ offer cannot simply be deferred to 13+. John Lyon provides separate 11+ and 13+ routes. None of these is an assured offer or bursary.

blocks.title: Read the second book directly on an iPad
body: The publisher and Apple Books list Michaela: The Power of Culture as an ebook. Apple Books provides a direct reading-app route; Hive separately identifies a DRM-protected EPUB, and the books page links the authorised PDF preview. The preview is not the full book.
No lawful full PDF/EPUB of the first book was verified. Catalogue metadata and print editions are linked rather than presented as working downloads.

blocks.title: Precise remaining questions, with a ready request
body: The implementation and recovery are complete, but public evidence does not settle every research question. Many exact arrival/departure dates and current jobs remain unknown. The complete current Year 7 timetable, full year-by-year subject schemes and the 2028 admission policy are not verified here. The alternatives page is a candidate shortlist, not an eligibility guarantee.

Suggested school enquiry: We are researching September 2028 entry. Please could you share a current Year 7 weekly timetable with lesson lengths; KS3 and KS4 subject maps/reading lists; current GCSE exam boards and specifications; typical weekly homework by year; music, art, DT and sport provision and participation arrangements; the relevant admissions policy when determined; and any publicly available current teaching-staff subject/qualification list? We are not requesting private HR or pupil data.
